reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch Re-Harden (mat_g1_na_q2_6), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The sampled problems directly satisfy the curriculum requirement to "Solve problems (given orally or in pictures) involving addition with sums up to 100 without regrouping." by presenting authentic addition word problems and linear step scenarios. Items such as "There are 52 trophies in one basket and 30 trophies in another basket. How many trophies are there in all?" and "Carlo had 84 canvases. Then Carlo got 0 more. How many canvases does Carlo have now?" require students to compute non-regrouping sums cleanly within 100.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The dataset spans the key sub-cases expected under this competency: single-digit counting on like "Start at 1. Count up 2 more. What number do you land on?", combining single digits with multiples of ten in "There is 1 score card in one basket and 10 score cards in another basket. How many score cards are there in all?", adding zero, and adding two-digit numbers with single digits as seen in "Pia collected 85 fish food packet and 2 hamster bedding pack at the veterinary clinic. How many items did Pia collect in total?".

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Sentence structures and story contexts are tightly tailored for Grade 1 Quarter 2 students. Problems use clear, familiar vocabulary and repetitive syntactic forms such as "One basket has 3 cookies. Another basket has 1 cookie. If you put all the cookies together, how many cookies are there?" and sequential movement prompts like "Moses is on step 2. Moses climbs up 2 more steps. What step is Moses on now?", ensuring cognitive load focuses on additive combining.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Multiple distinct situational contexts and problem structures are present across the sample set. These include static set-combination in "Des has 10 knee pads. A friend has 3 knee pads. If they put all their knee pads together, how many knee pads do they have in all?", discrete change/increase on steps in "Sir Ben is on step 2. Sir Ben climbs up 1 more step. What step is Sir Ben on now?", and number line counting progression in "Start at 2. Count up 1 more. What number do you land on?".

competency_alignment.rationale: All generated items cleanly target addition without regrouping without introducing extraneous arithmetic concepts or higher-grade mechanisms. From fundamental counting on in "Start at 1. Count up 3 more. What number do you land on?" to two-digit combining in "Isko has 12 medals. A friend has 1 medal. If they put all their medals together, how many medals do they have in all?", the difficulty progression adheres strictly to the target competency.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The numerical range is distributed appropriately across the target domain of "sums up to 100 without regrouping." Samples scale from single-digit sums like "One basket has 3 colored pencils. Another basket has 1 colored pencil. If you put all the colored pencils together, how many colored pencils are there?" (sum 4) up to two-digit sums approaching 100 like "There are 52 trophies in one basket and 30 trophies in another basket. How many trophies are there in all?" (sum 82).
